lines.trans: What a gangster's way to die. Everything is changing at a dizzying pace.
I had something to tell you—sorry to drop by so suddenly. Let me introduce you.
Nice to meet you. Here is the thirty million yen you so kindly arranged for her.
Thank you deeply for everything you did on her behalf.
Didn't I tell you before that you didn't need to pay the money back?
I am going to marry this man.
Congratulations. Hearing it straight from you like this makes it much easier for me to let go.

words.gram: Polite ます-form of auxiliary くる, showing a change developing over time.

lines.trans: Thank you—please be happy without fail.

words.gram: Adverbial noun used for strong emphasis.

lines.trans: Please protect her well. Make sure she is never hurt over having worked as an actress—that is the one thing I ask.
I will.
Take good care of yourself.

words.gram: Noun in the idiom 気が向く (feel like doing).

lines.trans: Damn it all! I loved her so much!

words.gram: Past tense of plain copula だ.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: respectful word for a person (かた)
meanings.note: Read かた, polite replacement for 人 (ひと) when announcing visitors or customers.

examples.text: あの方はどなたですか。

examples.trans: The person in charge has arrived.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: しかたないだろ！こんな状況ですぐに対応できるはずがない。
examples.trans: Give them a break! Nobody can adjust right away in a situation like this.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: Covers everything from a casual chat to a business deal or idea.

examples.trans: Let us have a little talk.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Casual/intimate apology, often softened with な or ね.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Adverbial form of 急 (sudden).

examples.trans: Calling me by my bare name all of a sudden, huh?

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Humble counterpart of もらう; volitional いただこう means 'let's take them / I'll have them'.

forms.title: Key forms of いただく

examples.text: お時間をいただけますか。
examples.trans: Could you spare me some time?

examples.text: 税金対策でプールしておいたギャラ三千万だ。
examples.trans: It's thirty million in appearance fees we set aside for tax purposes.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: 奈緒子のためにご尽力くださり、ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you deeply for everything you did on her behalf.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.note: First-person pronoun commonly used by men and boys in friendly or polite everyday settings.

examples.text: 僕もコーヒーをください。

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Polite/standard form of 金 (かね) with honorific prefix お.
Godan transitive verb.
Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.note: Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。
私この人と結婚するんだ。
examples.trans: I am going to marry this man.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

examples.text: 楽しみです。実はお伝えしたいことがあって。
examples.trans: I'm looking forward to it. Actually, there's something I wanted to tell you.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: 最後まで諦めないでください。
examples.trans: Please don't give up until the end.

examples.text: 夢を諦めたくありません。
examples.trans: I don't want to give up on my dream.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Adverbial noun used for strong certainty.

examples.text: 明日は絶対に来てください。

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。
この男は前科者ですよ！グループの事業に傷がつきますよ。
examples.trans: This man is an ex-convict! He will stain our group's businesses!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.note: In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

meanings.note: Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.

examples.text: ふざけんなよチキショー！好きだったんだよ！
examples.trans: Damn it all! I loved her so much!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Na-adjective; the thing liked is marked with が or は.

examples.text: どんな食べ物が好きですか。
examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
